subject: Post-demo: CascadeAI integration — auth, routing & streaming contract
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: CascadeAI integration — auth, routing & streaming contract

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the productive demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical workshop: 

Summary from our call
- Primary use case: user-facing chat assistant + a background reranker over domain embeddings (short docs).
- Scale target: ~500 concurrent users at launch, expect 1.2M tokens/day within month 2.
- SLOs: 95th p95 latency target of <250ms for short-turn chat, streaming acceptable for long responses.

Key integration/architecture points and asks
1) SDK & auth: we recommended Redwood SDK v1.8 (language agnostic). For auth you mentioned corporate preference for short-lived tokens. Options we discussed: API keys with rotation via Vault, OIDC-based token exchange (recommended), or mTLS for on-prem. Please confirm favoured approach so we can include concrete code snippets in the workshop.
2) Routing & model variants: plan to route production low-latency requests to a quantized LlamaX-8 variant and fallback to full-precision LlamaX-16 for high-quality responses. We need your decision on cost vs quality tradeoff and whether you want region-based routing (US/EU).
3) Structured output / tool calling: you said the assistant should return JSON with a `actions[]` array when a tool call is required. We'll provide a schema and sample tool-call DSL; confirm whether you want strict JSON-LD validation or a lightweight schema.
4) Embeddings & reranker: recommended embedding dimension 1024 with an FAISS index; initial reranker will use dense embeddings + lightweight cross-encoder fallback. We noted your index TTL and retention needs — please confirm retention window.
5) Request/response schema questions (chat vs completions): for chat flows we recommend the Chat API with explicit messages and streaming tokens enabled. For single-turn generation (bulk batch processing) use the Completions endpoint with deterministic sampling. Key knobs to decide now: `max_tokens` limits per role, stop sequences for safety, and whether you prefer server-side tokenization counts or client-side estimates.

Open items / asks from your side
- Confirm preferred auth (OIDC preferred on our side).
- Confirm whether streaming is required for the first release (affects SDK setup and websocket support).
- Share sample document set (~50 docs) and a representative short prompt so we can run embedding quality checks before the workshop.

Attachments: cascade_proposal_v1.pdf (commercial + SLA draft), auth_options_matrix.csv (matrix of auth choices), example_request_response_schema.json (draft schema for actions[] and tool calls).

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- Today: you confirm auth and streaming preference.
- Tues 2028-04-24: 90-min integration workshop (deep dive on SDK, auth handshake, routing).
- Fri 2028-04-28: Redwood-run embedding sample and preliminary reranker scores.

Thanks — I’ll schedule the workshop once you confirm the auth approach.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Marissa — great summary, really helpful. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) Auth: we prefer OIDC but need to understand token lifetime and whether Redwood supports token introspection / revocation hooks. Does the SDK handle automatic re-exchange?
2) Streaming: long-form responses are important for knowledge-base lookups; we’d like streaming for chat. Any impact on billed tokens or cost model we should be aware of?
3) Tokenization: our engineering team counts tokens client-side using tiktoken; curious if Redwood’s token accounting matches tiktoken exactly (we saw minor divergences on the demo).
4) Completions vs Chat: for multi-turn flows with system/user/assistant roles we’ll use Chat; but for some templated batch summaries we might use Completions — what differences should we expect for stop sequences semantics?

Also attaching a small set of example prompts/dev notes (separate email). Can you also share a short SDK snippet for OIDC handshake?

Thanks,
Sarah
CTO, CascadeAI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Yang <sarah.yang@cascadeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 14:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: CascadeAI integration — auth, routing & streaming contract

Hi Sarah — quick answers inline to help unblock your engs before the workshop.

1) Token lifecycle / OIDC: Redwood supports OIDC exchange (token exchange + refresh). SDKs (v1.8+) include a token provider interface — you can plug in your IdP to manage short-lived access tokens. We also provide introspection endpoints for enterprise customers and a webhook for revocation events (see auth_options_matrix.csv).

2) Streaming & billing: streaming does not change token billing semantics — charged per token emitted. Streaming reduces client-perceived latency but the token accounting is identical to non-streamed responses. For chunked responses tokens emitted are counted as they are produced.

3) Tokenization parity: we match tiktoken for the model families we run (we surface model-specific tokenizers). There are edge cases with custom tokenizers; for those we provide a tokenization preview endpoint in the SDK so you can validate counts pre-flight.

4) Stop sequences: Chat streaming supports a `stop` array applied server-side and enforced during generation; for Completions stop is similar but you may need to ensure your prompt framing (role separator) doesn't accidentally match your stop tokens. Short recommendation: use role-delimited chat messages for multi-turn and use stop sequences for deterministic single-turn completions.

5) Schema + tool calling: attached example_request_response_schema.json has a small example. For strict validation we can enable a JSON-LD context; otherwise lightweight JSON schema is quick and compatible with our tool-calling hooks. If you plan server-side validation, let us know the field-level requirements and we will turn on best-effort schema enforcement at the runtime (this will add a small validation latency).

Snippet: (pseudo-code)
``
// OIDC flow (JS SDK)
const tokenProvider = new OidcTokenProvider({ issuer: 'https://id.cascadeai.com', clientId: 'cascade-client' });
const client = new RedwoodClient({ tokenProvider });
await client.connect(); // handles exchange/refresh
``

Happy to walk through this in Tuesday's workshop. Marissa — I can prepare a live token exchange demo and a streaming example with Chrome devtools to show chunked frames.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
